justification.statement: jumbling-theory-card-6@491663cb04a1065a0e94a8300fd225991c6cba95:After an admissible letter at a cap, every letter at the same cap is admissible
justification.text: Card 6's statement of the theory draft's Propositions 1.2, 2.2 and 2.4, at the commit that last changed the card: A twist at a cap c turns the pieces inside H_c⁺, the cap's side of its cut, as one rigid body that maps H_c⁺ onto itself, and leaves every other piece in place, so it creates no straddler of c's cut. After an admissible letter at c, every letter at c is therefore admissible. The argument holds at the same cap only: a piece that the first letter takes off the lattice can straddle another cap's cut (card 6: pieces of height 2 can block grips of other classes).

steps.check: The named word has two letters, [0, 12] and [0, 45].

At solved no piece straddles cap 0's cut, so the first letter applies. Item 12 is a jumble (under I_a, items 0 to 11 are the retained rotations, item 0 the identity, and items 12 to 59 the jumbles), so after it cap 0's pieces are off the lattice, and the solved state no longer decides the second letter. A twist at a cap c moves only the pieces inside H_c⁺, rigidly within it, so it creates no straddler of c, and the second letter at the same cap 0 applies too: the word is admissible. The argument holds at the same cap only: card 6 shows that pieces of height 2 can block grips of other classes.
Item 45 is the inverse of item 12 at the same cap 0, so the second letter undoes the first: every piece is back on its pose, and 0 pieces are off the lattice after the word.
The named twist has one letter.
Its cap is the letter's first number, 7.
